title: Egg sandwich on griddle/pancake with meat

content.title: About
content.content: An egg sandwich on a griddle‑cooked pancake with meat is a hearty breakfast or light lunch consisting of a fried egg, grilled meat (usually ham or bacon) and a soft pancake cooked on a griddle. The sandwich combines the gentle flavor of eggs, the aroma of fried meat, and a subtle sweet note from the pancake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes cooked on a griddle develop a crisp edge and a light smoky flavor.
The tradition of pairing eggs and meat in one dish dates back to early American breakfasts of the 19th century.
For a healthier version, whole‑grain flour can be used for the pancake.
Adding fresh herbs (parsley, dill) boosts aroma and brightens the dish.
The sandwich is easy to wrap in foil or paper for on‑the‑go meals.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, while meat supplies niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Egg yolk is rich in lutein and zeaxanthin, antioxidants that protect the eyes.

items.title: Moderate carbs
items.content: A whole‑grain pancake provides slowly digestible carbohydrates, helping maintain stable blood sugar.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs and should substitute with alternative proteins.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed meats like ham or bacon can be salty; choose low‑sodium options when possible.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑rich due to butter in the pancake and fat in the meat; watch portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Eggs and meat must be fully cooked to avoid salmonella and campylobacter infections.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, cut in half. It can be eaten with hands or with a fork and knife. Add fresh vegetables (tomato, lettuce) or sauces (mustard, mayo) to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a skillet or microwave to prevent the pancake from becoming soggy.
